container_kinds.lifetime: frame checkpoint through terminal execution retention
v0.8 invocation creation through terminal execution retention
execution creation through terminal execution retention

container_kinds.owner: one explicitly authorized local data namespace

container_identity.identity_rule: kind, owner_id, and container_id form one stable case-sensitive identity
container_identity.revision_rule: every successful mutation increments one positive monotonic revision
container_identity.content_rule: content_digest covers canonical ordered variable identities and typed values

variable_contract.name_rule: bounded NFC identifier; ordinal case-sensitive uniqueness within the container

declared_type_mapping.mapping_rule: Each documented data-container declared type maps to exactly one canonical spell.data.value/1 type; reverse mapping is lossless and no numeric, time, or string coercion is implied.

operation_matrix.precondition: namespace CREATE authorization, explicit schema revision, create revision zero, and idempotency key
operation_matrix.effect: one empty durable container revision with audit and outbox evidence

operation_matrix.precondition: expected container revision and exact declared type
operation_matrix.effect: one atomic variable and container revision

operation_matrix.precondition: expected container revision and variable identity
authorized container read and bounded cursor

runtime_container_provisioning.authority: trusted execution admission and checkpoint services only
runtime_container_provisioning.rule: a public CREATE operation can create only DATA_CONTAINER and cannot forge an execution, frame, invocation, ARGS, or IVARS owner identity

args_rules: These ARGS rules apply only to IR and executions newly created under the v0.8 data contract.
Arguments are validated and committed atomically before v0.8 child execution admission.
For a v0.8-created invocation, ARGS is immutable after admission and never aliases a parent mutable value.
Missing required, extra, duplicate, or type-incompatible arguments reject admission without creating the child execution.
Every argument retains its canonical typed-value digest and caller provenance.
Accepted v0.6 and v0.7 IR, execution settings, safe-point mutation behavior, evidence, and release semantics are unchanged and are never retroactively interpreted by this v0.8 ARGS contract.
ivars_rules: IVARS is private to one execution instance and cannot be read through another execution identity.
Checkpoint settlement commits procedure state, IVARS mutations, and their revisions atomically.
A restart loads only the latest fully committed checkpoint and cannot replay a partial mutation.
data_container_rules: Persistent containers require an explicit namespace ACL and immutable schema revision.
Mutation requires compare-and-set against the authoritative container revision.
Enumeration is stable by ordinal variable_id and uses an opaque revision-bound cursor.
Deletion creates a durable tombstone; identity reuse requires a new container_id.

recovery_and_races.write_vs_write: exactly one matching expected revision commits; losers receive REVISION_CONFLICT
recovery_and_races.write_vs_delete: exactly one commits at the expected revision and the other observes the new revision or tombstone
recovery_and_races.checkpoint_vs_crash: visibility is all-or-nothing with the durable execution checkpoint
recovery_and_races.retry: an idempotency-bound committed mutation returns its original result without a second revision
recovery_and_races.corruption: digest mismatch returns CORRUPT_CONTAINER and exposes no decoded values

forbidden_capabilities: text, template, expression, function, module, or Python evaluation
object deserialization, callable storage, import, file handle, process handle, or socket
cross-owner aliasing or mutable reference sharing
host file, URL, network, GCS, mission-network, spacecraft, or legacy-adapter access
unbounded value, container, transaction, or enumeration size
